title: Knob consultation routing and commitment playbook for optimization requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly request targeted guidance (knobs, quantization recommendations, routing rules) rather than feature changes. Without a standardized intake+commitment playbook we (a) under-commit and miss SLAs, (b) over-commit engineering time to low-value requests, and (c) generate inconsistent advice across SE/PS/concierge.

Goal: Create a repeatable PM-run playbook that triages advisory requests for batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, and routing policies into three lanes (Self-serve guidance, Concierge advisory, Enterprise commitment). The playbook should define intake fields, SLA targets, qualification criteria, escalation triggers, required artifacts for engineering handoffs, and success metrics.

Scope: Non-bug optimization/advisory requests only (performance knobs, model/quantization recommendations, routing & fallback policies, autoscaling tuning). Excludes: feature requests, security issues, and infra incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Published public-facing intake form template for advisory requests (Confluence link) and internal intake form with required telemetry fields
Defined qualification checklist for Self-serve vs Concierge vs Enterprise lanes with examples
SLA targets documented: Self-serve (48h auto-response + KB link), Concierge (5 business days), Enterprise commitment (initial triage within 2 business days, scoping within 10 business days)
Handoff runbook for ENG containing required artifacts (repro prompt set, latency/cost dashboard link, recent model config, customer SLA)
Pilot run with two ongoing enterprise customers and measurement of TTR and customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT)
success_metrics: Time to first meaningful response (target: <48h for all lanes)
% of advisory requests solved with self-serve docs within 2 weeks (target: 35%)
Concierge-to-commitment conversion rate (target: 20% of concierge engagements become scoped commitments)
Average engineering hours per advisory (target: <12h for concierge, scoped separately for commitments)
runbook_steps: 1) Intake: Customer fills public intake form or SE opens internal ticket. Required fields: workload profile, token throughput, tail-latency SLO, request logs link (or sample), current model+quant config, business impact description
2) Auto-qualification: Backend rules classify request based on throughput, data sensitivity, and SLA. If rules match self-serve patterns, return KB links and close with tracking tag
3) Triage: PM reviews within SLA. If candidate for Concierge, assign specialist (solutions engineer) and schedule 1:1 diagnostic call
4) Diagnostic: Collect reproducible prompt set, perf traces, and cost breakdowns. Run small-scale repro with suggested knobs (batch size adjustments, prefix/KV cache hints, quant profile variants)
5) Recommendation: Produce formal advisory note (config delta + validation checklist) and share with customer. If changes risk model quality > threshold, require A/B eval and eng signoff
6) Escalation: If advisory requires persistent infra changes, model retraining, or SLA-backed capacity, move to Enterprise Commitment lane with scoping sprint and estimated PO/AP commitment
7) Close & Learn: Post-engagement survey + internal blameless writeup with reproducible artifacts saved to the optimization playbook
escalation_matrix: Self-serve lane: low-throughput or common patterns (cache/batch knobs). SLA: auto-response within 48h. Owner: Docs + DSE.

Concierge lane: mid-impact customers or uncommon configurations requiring SE tuning. SLA: initial contact in 5 business days, advisory delivered in 10 business days. Owner: Solutions Engineering + PM.

Enterprise Commitment lane: high-impact/contracted customers or requests requiring infra/model changes. SLA: initial triage within 2 business days, scope doc & resource commitment within 10 business days. Owner: PM + ENG lead + AE
required_artifacts: Repro prompt set (min 5 examples) and expected outputs
Token and latency distribution dashboard link (observability console) - e.g. https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/abcd-optimization
Cost-per-token baseline and desired reduction target
Current model and quantization config (model ID + flags) and recent rollout notes
Relevant GitHub PRs or infra change requests (e.g. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234)

open_questions: How strict should the engineering hours cap be for Concierge engagements before forcing a paid scoping ticket?
What level of telemetry access can enterprise customers provide (privacy/compliance constraints) for reproducible traces?
Do we require an explicit legal addendum for optimization commitments that include changes to model quantization or routing fallbacks?
